must_remember: A coaxial optical system has six cardinal points: two principal foci ($F_1, F_2$), two principal points ($H_1, H_2$), and two nodal points ($N_1, N_2$).
Principal planes are conjugate planes with a transverse magnification of $m = +1$.
Newton's formula for a coaxial optical system is given by $x_1 x_2 = f_1 f_2$, where distances are measured from the principal foci.
The ratio of focal lengths is related to the initial and final refractive indices by $\frac{f_1}{f_2} = -\frac{\mu_1}{\mu_2}$.
Nodal points coincide with principal points if and only if the refractive index of the medium on both sides of the system is the same.

glossary.meaning: An axial point for which rays starting from it emerge parallel to the principal axis after refraction.
An axial point where rays parallel to the principal axis incident on the system converge or appear to diverge from after refraction.
A pair of conjugate planes on the optical axis for which the transverse magnification is +1.
A pair of conjugate points on the axis having an angular magnification of +1.

comparisons.title: Principal Points vs. Nodal Points
rows: Always distinct unless $\mu_1 = \mu_2$ and focal lengths equal
